howDoI.q: How do I make a die that rolls?
How do I make something change again and again?
How do I stop it with a touch?
How do I leave something to chance?
How do I make a roll pick the door?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Roll the Dice is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the level that say what you are looking at. It has one short level and nothing in it can cost a life.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the level is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Up and Down climb a ladder. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score.

A die rolls on the ground. Touch it and it stops, and the face it stops on picks the door.

pages.head: Level: Roll the Dice
pages.html:
Roll the Dice

A die sits on the ground, showing a new face about every half second. Walk into it and it stops on the face it shows, and gives you a key: gold for an odd face (1, 3 or 5), silver for an even one (2, 4 or 6). The stopped die has a colored rim, gold or blue, so you can see which key you got.

Ahead a wall has two doors. The gold door is on the ground. The silver door is up a ladder. A door stays shut without its key, so the face picks the door. Try the wrong one first and you will see.

There are four coins past the wall, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the level is made

  • A die is a ring of blocks. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor and pick face1. Its Next block is face2 and its Time is 10 ticks. face2 turns into face3, and so on up to face6, whose Next block is face1. Because the last block points back to the first, the die goes round for ever. There are 18.2 ticks in a second.
  • One block on the map. The map holds a single face1. A block's timer changes every block of that kind on the same tick, so the map would show the same face everywhere. One die needs one cell.
  • A touch stops it. Each face has a Touched block: face1 is touched into stop1, a copy with no Next block, so it never changes again. A touched block changes the map cell for good, and it shows whichever face the ring was on at that moment.
  • A face gives a key. Each face block has an Effect counter: the odd faces add 1 to counter 20 (gold keys) and the even faces add 1 to counter 21 (silver keys). Touching it again does nothing, because it is now a stop block.
  • The doors. gate is solid, and its Effect counter takes 1 from the gold keys and then goes away. gateSilver does the same for the silver keys. With no key, the door stays shut.
  • The way over is closed. Brick fills the wall above and between the doors, so Mara cannot jump over. A hedge closes the room in at both ends.
  • The clock starts with the level. The ring is set going when the scene loads. The face you meet depends on the tick you touch it.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A die in Game-Maker is a ring of blocks that turn into each other. Some things you may expect are not there:

  • It has no random number. The ring turns at the same speed every time, so the face you stop on depends only on the tick you touch it. The same walk gives the same roll, and a player who waits a little longer gets a different one. Chance here means timing.
  • It cannot roll when the player does something. The ring starts when the room loads and nothing Mara does can start it, so the die is already rolling when he arrives.
  • One block makes one die. Every block of a kind changes on the same tick, so two dice from the same ring would show the same face. A second die needs its own ring.
  • It cannot add up a roll. A touch changes one counter by a fixed amount, so each face gives a key rather than a number.
  • A door cannot look at the die. It only checks that you carry the key.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.bbl, change face1's Time from 10 to 40 to give the die a slower roll. Change the other faces too, or one face will stay up longer than the rest.
  • Make every face's Time 3 and the die is hard to stop on a number you want.
  • Change face3's Effect counter from 20 to 21, and a 3 gives a silver key.
  • Draw your own die faces in the blocks editor.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
